newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Placer Dome sees 2.3m oz gold output.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Placer Dome sees 2.3m oz gold output.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said on Tuesday it expects its share of gold production to increase to about 2.3 million ounces in 1997, from 1.9 million ounces this year, at a cash production cost of around US$240 an ounce.
The increase assumes completion of the proposed acquisitions of Highlands Gold Ltd and Placer Pacific Ltd, Placer Dome said.
Without the acquisitions, the 1997 share of production will be about two million ounces at a cash production cost of some US$235 an ounce, the company said.
The estimates also take into account the sale if the Kiena and Sigma mines by the end of the first quarter of 1997, Placer Dome said.
Vancouver-based Placer Dome is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange. It is also listed on the Australian Stock Exchange.

Placer Dome on Monday revised an offer it is making for Highlands, saying it was willing to cancel its interest in Highlands and instead pay A$276.8 million for Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea.
Placer Dome has about 33 percent of Highlands.
Both companies have 25 percent stakes in Porgera, Placer's being held through its listed Placer Pacific Ltd unit. It is bidding for the shares in Placer Pacific not already held.
Placer Dome said its share of production from Placer Pacific is expected to be 10 percent above 1996's 90,000 ounces at an average cash production cost of about US$280 an ounce.
Cash production costs are expected to be higher due principally to lower ore grades at the Misima and Porgera mines, it said.
Gold output from the U.S. operations of Placer Dome is anticipated by the company to increase by about 45 percent to 450,000 ounces at a cash production cost of less than US$200 an ounce.
Highlands said earlier on Tuesday it would respond to the latest offer by Placer Dome by January 6, 1997.
